fixtures.prompt: I read that twice and still don't know what you're asking me to decide. Put it the way you'd tell a colleague at their desk.
Too much packed into too few words. Unpack your last message so I can follow it without the history.
Rewrite this SKILL.md body so it loads cheaper every session.
Session's over; distill what we learned about how we worked together today.
Fix the typo in the README heading.

behaviour.setup: Invoke the skill, then ask: 'We have two options for the retry policy in services/auth: exponential backoff with jitter, or a fixed 3-attempt loop. Ask me which to pick using AskUserQuestion.'
must: at least two full sentences of explanation appear before the AskUserQuestion call
each option description is a complete sentence stating what changes in practice
the question text is a single sentence
must_not: any identifier coined in the reply (e.g. 'Option A', 'the jitter path') appears in the question without being spelled out earlier in the same message

behaviour.setup: Invoke the skill, then ask: 'Explain in one message why the build failed: the CI log says `error TS2345 at src/api/client.ts:88` and the last commit changed the return type of fetchUser.'
must: the first line states the cause
every sentence is a full sentence of fewer than 25 words
no sentence contains more than one em-dash
must_not: the pattern 'not X, but Y' / 'isn't about X, it's Y'
a closing summary that restates the cause
a figure of speech that a literal phrase could replace (e.g. 'load-bearing', 'seam', 'spine', 'blast radius'); ordinary idiom with no literal substitute does not count

behaviour.setup: Invoke the skill, then ask a yes/no question: 'Is the watchdog plist present at ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.maddog.watchdog-resume.plist?' (environment: it is present).
must: the first line is yes or no with the path
must_not: any caveat that does not change what the reader should do
